title: Leave, Steer, Arrive: The Puzzle Solved

scenes.visual: Title card: Leave, Steer, Arrive: The Puzzle Solved.

scenes.tts: How does a crest cell let go and find its way? And what happens when a step fails?
scenes.visual: Three icons in a row: a released cell, a forked path, a broken link.
scenes.narration: How does a crest cell let go and find its way? And what happens when a step fails?

scenes.tts: To leave, a crest cell must loosen its grip. In chick, a cadherin called cadherin six B helps hold it to its neighbours.
scenes.caption: To leave, a crest cell must loosen its grip. In chick, a cadherin called Cadherin-6B helps hold it to its neighbours.
scenes.visual: Gold cells held together by small clasps labelled Cadherin-6B. Corner label, kept through scene s07: chick experiments.
scenes.narration: To leave, a crest cell must loosen its grip. In chick, a cadherin called Cadherin-6B helps hold it to its neighbours.

scenes.tts: A transcription factor, snail two, is needed. Block it, and fewer cells leave.
scenes.caption: A transcription factor, Snail2, is needed. Block it, and fewer cells leave.
scenes.visual: Label Snail2 in the nucleus; when it is crossed out, fewer cells leave.
scenes.narration: A transcription factor, Snail2, is needed. Block it, and fewer cells leave.

scenes.tts: Suppose snail two works by switching off cadherin six B. Lower snail two. What happens to cadherin six B?
scenes.caption: Suppose Snail2 works by switching off Cadherin-6B. Lower Snail2. What happens to Cadherin-6B?
scenes.visual: Predict card: Snail2 lowered; Cadherin-6B RNA, up or down?
scenes.narration: Suppose Snail2 works by switching off Cadherin-6B. Lower Snail2. What happens to Cadherin-6B?

scenes.tts: Cadherin six B RNA rises within about half an hour, just as predicted. The authors concluded snail two represses it directly.
scenes.caption: Cadherin-6B RNA rises within about half an hour, just as predicted. The authors concluded Snail2 represses it directly.
scenes.visual: A bar for Cadherin-6B RNA climbs; Snail2 shown binding the Cadherin-6B gene. Note: about half an hour.
scenes.narration: Cadherin-6B RNA rises within about half an hour, just as predicted. The authors concluded Snail2 represses it directly.

scenes.tts: Lower cadherin six B instead, and cells leave early. It is a brake. Snail two probably lifts it, at least partly.
scenes.caption: Lower Cadherin-6B instead, and cells leave early. It is a brake. Snail2 probably lifts it, at least partly.
scenes.visual: Three-row table: control, Snail2 lowered, Cadherin-6B lowered, with departure normal, reduced, early.
scenes.narration: Lower Cadherin-6B instead, and cells leave early. It is a brake. Snail2 probably lifts it, at least partly.

scenes.tts: Now steering. In the chick trunk, crest cells pass only through the front half of each sclerotome.
scenes.visual: Trunk side view: crest streams pass through the front half of each block; back halves tinted red.
scenes.narration: Now steering. In the chick trunk, crest cells pass only through the front half of each sclerotome.

scenes.tts: The back half repels them on contact. In chick, ephrin B is one such signal.
scenes.caption: The back half repels them on contact. In chick, ephrin-B is one such signal.
scenes.visual: A crest cell touches a red back-half cell and retreats. Label: ephrin-B (chick studies).
scenes.narration: The back half repels them on contact. In chick, ephrin-B is one such signal.

scenes.tts: In mouse, semaphorin three F also repels them. Neither is known to be the only cue.
scenes.caption: In mouse, semaphorin 3F also repels them. Neither is known to be the only cue.
scenes.visual: A second label appears beside the first: semaphorin 3F (mouse studies). Both labels stay on screen.
scenes.narration: In mouse, semaphorin 3F also repels them. Neither is known to be the only cue.

scenes.tts: Crest cells also steer each other. When two touch, they collapse protrusions at the contact and move apart. Edge cells tend to move outward.
scenes.visual: Two cells meet, collapse protrusions at the contact and move apart.
scenes.narration: Crest cells also steer each other. When two touch, they collapse protrusions at the contact and move apart. Edge cells tend to move outward.

scenes.tts: Mutual attraction holds the group together, and a chemokine gives it direction.
scenes.visual: Recipe card with three lines: contact pushes apart, attraction holds, chemokine steers.
scenes.narration: Mutual attraction holds the group together, and a chemokine gives it direction.

scenes.tts: In frogs, a cluster follows that chemokine better than a lone cell. For trunk crest, this is less clear.
scenes.visual: A cluster climbs a gradient; a lone cell wanders. Note: frog cranial crest; less clear for trunk crest of birds and mammals.
scenes.narration: In frogs, a cluster follows that chemokine better than a lone cell. For trunk crest, this is less clear.

scenes.tts: Now the puzzle. The patient has Waardenburg syndrome type four.
scenes.caption: Now the puzzle. The patient has Waardenburg syndrome type 4.
scenes.visual: The puzzle returns from the corner: gut, forelock, ear. Label: Waardenburg syndrome type 4.
scenes.narration: Now the puzzle. The patient has Waardenburg syndrome type 4.

scenes.tts: The genes are sox ten, the endothelin receptor B, and endothelin three.
scenes.caption: The genes are SOX10, the endothelin receptor B (EDNRB), and EDN3.
scenes.visual: EDN3 drawn as a signal sent to EDNRB receptors on both enteric precursors and melanocytes, with SOX10 shown inside both lineages.
scenes.narration: The genes are SOX10, the endothelin receptor B (EDNRB), and EDN3.

scenes.tts: Enteric precursors need them, and so do melanocytes, including those the inner ear needs for hearing.
scenes.visual: A wire from the genes to the inner ear; both lineages dim when one gene is cut.
scenes.narration: Enteric precursors need them, and so do melanocytes, including those the inner ear needs for hearing.

scenes.tts: Try a toy model. One front moves down the gut from the mouth end, within a fixed time. Slow it. Which part stays empty?
scenes.visual: Label: toy model, one-front approximation; real routes are more complex. A gold front advances along the gut from the mouth end; a clock runs down. Predict card.
scenes.narration: Try a toy model. One front moves down the gut from the mouth end, within a fixed time. Slow it. Which part stays empty?

scenes.tts: The end the front reaches last, the anal end. In the model, that segment is left without neurons.
scenes.visual: The slowed front stops short; the last segment stays grey.
scenes.narration: The end the front reaches last, the anal end. In the model, that segment is left without neurons.

scenes.tts: That is a toy model. In the clinic, too, the empty segment usually starts at the anal end. Rare cases skip a segment.
scenes.visual: Note on screen: toy model. Then a clinical sketch labelled typical pattern, with the grey segment starting at the anus.
scenes.narration: That is a toy model. In the clinic, too, the empty segment usually starts at the anal end. Rare cases skip a segment.

scenes.tts: An earlier failed step need not mean wider damage. Treacher Collins syndrome cuts crest numbers early. Yet it mainly affects the face, ears and eyelids.
scenes.visual: Treacher Collins: an early loss of cranial crest, linked to the jaw, cheekbones, ears and eyelids. Label: regional vulnerability. No ranking of steps.
scenes.narration: An earlier failed step need not mean wider damage. Treacher Collins syndrome cuts crest numbers early. Yet it mainly affects the face, ears and eyelids.

scenes.tts: Tissues that fail together often share a requirement. Which tissues fail depends on where the gene is needed, the variant, and each tissue's sensitivity.
scenes.visual: Closing card: fail together, often share a requirement.
scenes.narration: Tissues that fail together often share a requirement. Which tissues fail depends on where the gene is needed, the variant, and each tissue's sensitivity.

scenes.tts: One border, many destinations. The start biases the options, and the journey helps choose.
scenes.visual: The guiding-idea card returns.
scenes.narration: One border, many destinations. The start biases the options, and the journey helps choose.
